--- title: "A/B Testing: Statistics as a Product Decision System" description: "Design experiments from randomization through lift, uncertainty, sample size, guardrails and decision-making." author: "MLStation" date: 2026-10-01 categories: [Statistics, Experimentation, A/B Testing, Data Science] draft: false --- A/B testing is where probability, sampling, confidence intervals and hypothesis tests become an operational decision system. The statistical calculation is only one part. ::: {.callout-tip} ## What you will learn - Randomization and treatment/control groups - Absolute and relative lift - Difference-in-proportions uncertainty - Sample size, power and minimum detectable effect - Guardrails, peeking and practical decisions ::: ## The causal engine: randomization ```text Eligible users ↓ random assignment ┌────┴────┐ A B control treatment └────┬────┘ ↓ compare outcomes ``` Randomization aims to make treatment assignment independent of pre-treatment characteristics, allowing differences in outcomes to be attributed to treatment **in expectation**. ## Interactive experiment simulator ```{ojs} //| echo: false viewof nab = Inputs.range([100,20000], {value:2000, step:100, label:"Users per group"}) viewof liftab = Inputs.range([0,.05], {value:.01, step:.0025, label:"Absolute treatment lift"}) rab=d3.randomLcg(.87) pA=.10; pB=pA+liftab convA=d3.sum(d3.range(nab),()=>rab()rab() A${(100*rateA).toFixed(2)}% B${(100*rateB).toFixed(2)}% Observed lift${(100*diff).toFixed(2)} pp ` ``` Repeat mentally by moving $n$: small experiments are noisy enough that B can lose even when its true conversion rate is higher. ## Absolute vs. relative lift If conversion moves from 10% to 11%: $$ \text{absolute lift}=11\%-10\%=1\text{ percentage point} $$ $$ \text{relative lift}=\frac{11\%-10\%}{10\%}=10\%. $$ Always state which one you mean. ## Simulation: the distribution of observed lift ::: {#5ac7f527 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="true"} import numpy as np, pandas as pd import plotly.express as px rng=np.random.default_rng(21) pA,pB=.10,.11 rows=[] for n in [200,1000,5000,20000]: for _ in range(1200): a=rng.binomial(n,pA)/n b=rng.binomial(n,pB)/n rows.append({"n":n,"lift":b-a}) df=pd.DataFrame(rows) fig=px.histogram(df,x="lift",animation_frame="n",nbins=50, range_x=[-.08,.10],histnorm="probability density") fig.add_vline(x=.01,line_dash="dash") fig.update_layout(height=380) fig.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Guardrails A primary metric can improve while the product gets worse elsewhere. ```text Primary: conversion ↑ Guardrails: latency? cancellations? refunds? retention? errors? ``` Predefine important metrics and decision rules. ## DS/ML Bridge Experiments evaluate not only UI changes but also ML systems: ```text ranking model recommendation algorithm search relevance model fraud threshold notification policy AI assistant experience ``` Offline metrics tell you what happened on a dataset. Randomized online experiments can measure the **causal product impact** of deploying the change. ::: {.callout-warning} ## Repeated peeking changes error behavior Running a fixed-horizon test but stopping whenever $p<0.05$ is not the same procedure you originally calibrated. Use a planned fixed horizon or an appropriate sequential method. ::: ## What should you save? ```text experiment/ ├── hypothesis.md ├── metric_definitions.json ├── sample_size_plan.json ├── assignment_version.json ├── analysis.ipynb └── decision.md ``` Pre-experiment decisions are valuable evidence against post-hoc storytelling. ## Summary - Randomization is the foundation of causal interpretation. - Lift must be accompanied by uncertainty. - Sample size should be tied to baseline rate, effect size, alpha and power. - Guardrails prevent optimizing one metric at the expense of the system. - A/B tests connect statistical inference directly to product decisions. **Next:** *Correlation, Confounding & Causality*
